name: Filter On. Answers Gone.
question: How do you build an AI search agent that respects user roles and still finds the right document?
problem: You added a role filter to your company's AI search agent so interns can't see salaries. An intern asks whether she can carry over unused leave, the five closest documents are all manager policies, the filter removes them, and the agent says "no policy found".
points: Put the role filter inside the first query, before any top-k. For the intern, WHERE runs before LIMIT.

title: How to Build an AI Search Agent That Respects User Roles — Role Filters, Top-K and Rerankers in RAG #shorts
caption:
ENGINEERING · How do you build an AI search agent that respects user roles and still finds the right document?

You added a role filter so interns can't see salaries. Now interns get empty answers.

An intern asks: can I carry over unused leave? The agent's vector search pulls the 5 closest documents. All 5 are manager policies. Then the role filter removes them. Nothing is left, so the agent says "no policy found". In SQL, that's LIMIT before WHERE.

Move the filter first and the intern's leave policy survives. It ranks 11th. Vector search turned every document into an embedding before anyone asked, so "carry over" and "leave encashment" sit close together. The top-5 cut drops it again.

That's the job of a reranker. Fetch 50 with the cheap vector search. The reranker reads the question and each document together and picks the 5. It sees "carry over" in both, and the policy moves to the top. It costs one model call per document, so it runs on 50, not the whole library.

3 rules for any RAG system with permissions:

1. Put the role filter inside the first query, before any top-k. For the intern, WHERE runs before LIMIT.
2. Fetch wide with the cheap search, then sort again before the cut. For the intern, 50 in, 5 out.
3. Log the cited document's rank before reranking. If it keeps arriving near 50, widen the first stage.

A document that ranks below 50 in the first search never reaches the reranker.

Save this for your next RAG design review. Send it to whoever owns your search agent's access control.

Blueprint is in the open vault. Link in bio.

sources: Bi-encoder retrieval (document vectors made before the query) vs cross-encoder reranking (one forward pass per question-document pair), and post-filtering after approximate top-k returning fewer than k results: standard retrieval behaviour, not a single cited source. 5, 11th and 50 are scene numbers.
